headline: Sell TSM and AMZN now, stage out of AVGO and NVDA, buy VRT, LLY, SNOW.
approach: We sell what the target book does not want first — TSM and AMZN outright, then AVGO and NVDA in halves so we never dump a big position in one day. Each sale funds the very next buy, biggest allocation gap first: compute power, then healthcare, then data. Nothing moves to the next step until the prior sale has settled and the cash is actually in the account.
first_move: Sell all $619 of TSM at market today, then place a $1,040 VRT buy order at $259.93.

steps.sell: Sell all $619 of TSM at market.
steps.why: Closes the single biggest hole in the book, compute power, using cash plus the TSM proceeds.
steps.realizes: Books a short-term loss on TSM that offsets your most expensive gains; no TSM rebuy for 30 days.

steps.trigger: VRT order is filled and TSM cash has settled
steps.sell: Sell all $633 of AMZN at market.
steps.why: Adds a healthcare earner whose demand does not care what the AI cycle does.
steps.realizes: Books a loss on AMZN you can use against gains; don't rebuy AMZN for 30 days.

steps.trigger: AVGO recovers its 4.7% loss back to your break-even price
steps.sell: Sell $680 of AVGO, about half the position.
steps.why: Halves your largest chip overweight into strength rather than at a low.
steps.realizes: Books half of AVGO's short-term loss against gains; no AVGO rebuy for 30 days.

steps.trigger: AVGO holds at or above the step 3 sale price for a week
steps.sell: Sell the remaining $683 of AVGO at market.
steps.why: Finishes the AVGO exit and swaps into a cheaper chipmaker tied to power and autos.
steps.realizes: Books the rest of AVGO's short-term loss; the 30-day no-rebuy clock restarts today.

steps.trigger: NVDA recovers its 2.5% loss back to your break-even price
steps.why: Starts cutting the concentration while keeping most of your best AI name intact.
steps.realizes: Books a small short-term loss on NVDA against gains; no NVDA rebuy for 30 days.

steps.trigger: Steps 1 through 5 are all filled and NVDA is still near break-even
steps.sell: Trim another $500 of NVDA at market.
steps.why: Finishes the trim and opens a small speculative sleeve with a hard exit already set.
steps.realizes: Books the second slice of NVDA's short-term loss; leaves roughly $1,000 cash for APLD, SMR and SOUN later.

guardrails: Stop selling AVGO or NVDA if they keep falling and no bounce comes — never sell quality at its low.
Do not rebuy TSM, AMZN, AVGO or NVDA within 30 days, or the tax loss is cancelled.
Pause all buying if the whole market drops hard; let it steady before spending the next dollar.
Cut SMCI at $21 and keep every speculative buy under $400 — that sleeve never gets averaged down.

tax.detail: Selling books a loss you can use to offset gains — short-term, which offsets the most expensive gains first. Don't rebuy within 30 days or the loss is disallowed.

Buy $660 of LLY near $1,226.54 — obesity drug demand that ignores the tech cycle.
Buy $570 of SNOW near $256.22 — AI is useless without the company data it stores.
Buy $475 of ON near $83.76 — cheap chipmaker tied to power management and autos.
Buy $475 of NU near $14.62 — fast-growing digital bank at a cheap price.

Speculative: buy $375 of APLD near $26.05, stop $19 — small AI data-center builder.
